name: Electron as a particle
statement: Is the matter in cathode rays a particle lighter than any atom?
status_source: Timeline of particle discoveries: "Electron discovered by J. J. Thomson"

name: Nature of uranium alpha radiation
statement: What is the weakly penetrating radiation emitted by uranium?
status_source: Timeline of particle discoveries: "Alpha particle discovered by Ernest Rutherford in uranium radiation"

name: Gamma radiation from uranium decay
statement: Does uranium decay emit a radiation more penetrating than alpha and beta rays?
status_source: Timeline of particle discoveries: "Gamma ray (a high-energy photon) discovered by Paul Villard in uranium decay"

name: Infrared radiation from the Sun
statement: Does sunlight carry invisible heat rays beyond the red end of the spectrum?
status_source: Timeline of particle discoveries: "William Herschel discovers 'heat rays' (now known as infrared)"

name: Ultraviolet radiation beyond violet light
statement: Do invisible rays exist beyond the violet end of the visible spectrum?
status_source: Timeline of particle discoveries: "Johann Wilhelm Ritter made the hallmark observation that invisible rays just beyond the violet end"

name: Penetrating rays from cathode ray tubes
statement: What are the penetrating rays produced when electron beams strike matter?
status_source: Timeline of particle discoveries: "X-ray produced by Wilhelm Roentgen (later identified as photons)"

name: Atomic nucleus
statement: Is the positive charge of the atom concentrated in a small central nucleus?
status_source: Timeline of particle discoveries: "Atomic nucleus identified by Ernest Rutherford, based on scattering observed by Hans Geiger and Ernest Marsden"

name: Proton as a nuclear constituent
statement: Does the nucleus contain a positively charged particle that is the hydrogen nucleus?
status_source: Timeline of particle discoveries: "Proton discovered by Ernest Rutherford"

name: Heavy hydrogen
statement: Is there a heavier isotope of hydrogen with a nucleus of two particles?
status_source: Timeline of particle discoveries: "Deuteron discovered by Harold Urey (predicted by Rutherford in 1920)"

name: Neutron
statement: Does the nucleus contain an electrically neutral particle with about the proton mass?
status_source: Timeline of particle discoveries: "Neutron discovered by James Chadwick (predicted by Rutherford in 1920)"

name: Existence of antimatter
statement: Does the positive counterpart of the electron predicted by the Dirac equation exist?
status_source: Timeline of particle discoveries: "Antielectron (or positron), the first antiparticle, discovered by Carl D. Anderson"

name: Penetrating cosmic-ray particle
statement: What is the penetrating cosmic-ray particle with a mass between the electron and the proton?
status_source: Timeline of particle discoveries: "Muon (or mu lepton) discovered by Seth Neddermeyer, Carl D. Anderson, J.C. Street, and E.C. Stevenson"

name: Carrier of the nuclear force
statement: Does the meson predicted by Yukawa to carry the nuclear force exist?
status_source: Timeline of particle discoveries: "Pion (or pi meson) discovered by C. F. Powell's group"

name: Strange particles
statement: Do cosmic rays contain particles that form fast and decay slowly?
status_source: Timeline of particle discoveries: "Kaon (or K meson), the first strange particle, discovered by George Dixon Rochester and Clifford Charles Butler"

name: Antiproton
statement: Does the proton have an antiparticle?
status_source: Timeline of particle discoveries: "Antiproton discovered by Owen Chamberlain, Emilio Segre, Clyde Wiegand, and Thomas Ypsilantis"

name: Detecting the neutrino
statement: Can the neutrino proposed to save energy conservation in beta decay be detected?
status_source: Timeline of particle discoveries: "Electron neutrino detected by Frederick Reines and Clyde Cowan"

name: Second kind of neutrino
statement: Is the neutrino paired with the muon distinct from the electron neutrino?
status_source: Timeline of particle discoveries: "Muon neutrino (or mu neutrino) shown to be distinct from the electron neutrino by a group headed by Leon Lederman"

name: Omega baryon
statement: Does the Omega baryon required by the eightfold classification of hadrons exist?
status_source: Timeline of particle discoveries: "Omega baryon and Xi baryon discovery at Brookhaven National Laboratory"

name: Internal structure of the proton
statement: Do protons contain point-like internal constituents?
status_source: Timeline of particle discoveries: "Partons (internal constituents of hadrons) observed in deep inelastic scattering experiments"

name: Charm quark
statement: Does a fourth quark flavour called charm exist?
status_source: Timeline of particle discoveries: "J/psi meson discovered by groups headed by Burton Richter and Samuel Ting, demonstrating the existence of the charm quark"

name: Third charged lepton
statement: Is there a charged lepton heavier than the muon?
status_source: Timeline of particle discoveries: "Tau discovered by a group headed by Martin Perl"

name: Bottom quark
statement: Does a fifth quark flavour called bottom exist?
status_source: Timeline of particle discoveries: "Upsilon meson discovered at Fermilab, demonstrating the existence of the bottom quark"

name: Carrier of the strong force
statement: Can the carrier of the strong force be seen in particle jets?
status_source: Timeline of particle discoveries: "Gluon observed indirectly in three-jet events at DESY"

name: Weak force carriers
statement: Do the W and Z bosons of the electroweak theory exist?
status_source: Timeline of particle discoveries: "W and Z bosons discovered by Carlo Rubbia, Simon van der Meer, and the CERN UA1 collaboration"

name: Top quark
statement: Does the sixth quark, the top quark, exist?
status_source: Timeline of particle discoveries: "Top quark discovered at Fermilab"

name: Antihydrogen atoms
statement: Can atoms of antimatter be made and measured?
status_source: Timeline of particle discoveries: "Antihydrogen produced and measured by the LEAR experiment at CERN"

name: Quark-gluon matter
statement: Can a quark-gluon fireball be made in heavy-ion collisions?
status_source: Timeline of particle discoveries: "Quark-gluon fireball discovered at CERN"

name: Tau neutrino
statement: Can the tau neutrino be observed directly?
status_source: Timeline of particle discoveries: "Tau neutrino first observed directly at Fermilab"

name: Antihelium nuclei
statement: Can antihelium-4 nuclei be produced and measured?
status_source: Timeline of particle discoveries: "Antihelium-4 produced and measured by the STAR detector"

name: Radioactivity of uranium
statement: Do uranium salts emit penetrating radiation without exposure to light?
status_source: Timeline of atomic and subatomic physics: "Antoine Henri Becquerel discovers the radioactivity of uranium"

name: Radioactive elements in pitchblende
statement: Why is pitchblende more radioactive than the uranium it contains?
status_source: Timeline of atomic and subatomic physics: "Marie and Pierre Curie discovered the existence of the radioactive elements radium and polonium"

name: Photoelectron energy law
statement: How does the maximum energy of photoelectrons depend on light intensity and frequency?
status_source: Timeline of atomic and subatomic physics: "Philipp Lenard observes that maximum photoelectron energies are independent of illuminating intensity but depend on frequency"

name: Characteristic X-rays of elements
statement: Does each element emit its own characteristic X-rays?
status_source: Timeline of atomic and subatomic physics: "Charles Barkla discovers that each element has a characteristic X-ray"

name: Composition of alpha particles
statement: What are alpha particles made of?
status_source: Timeline of atomic and subatomic physics: "Ernest Rutherford and Thomas Royds demonstrate that alpha particles are doubly ionized helium atoms"

name: Charge of the electron
statement: What is the fundamental unit of electric charge?
status_source: Timeline of atomic and subatomic physics: "Robert Millikan measures the fundamental unit of electric charge"

name: Stark splitting of hydrogen lines
statement: Do strong electric fields split the spectral lines of hydrogen?
status_source: Timeline of atomic and subatomic physics: "Johannes Stark demonstrates that strong electric fields will split the Balmer spectral line series of hydrogen"

name: Quantization of spin in space
statement: Is the orientation of atomic angular momentum quantized in space?
status_source: Timeline of atomic and subatomic physics: "Otto Stern and Walther Gerlach show 'spin quantization'"

name: Wave equation of quantum mechanics
statement: What wave equation governs the evolution of a quantum system?
status_source: Timeline of atomic and subatomic physics: "Erwin Schroedinger states his nonrelativistic quantum wave equation and formulates quantum wave mechanics"

name: Relativistic electron equation
statement: Can a relativistic wave equation for the electron be written that agrees with quantum mechanics?
status_source: Timeline of atomic and subatomic physics: "Paul Dirac states the Dirac equation"

name: Continuous beta decay spectrum
statement: Why do electrons from beta decay show a continuous energy spectrum?
status_source: Timeline of atomic and subatomic physics: "Wolfgang Pauli postulated the neutrino to explain the energy spectrum of beta decays"

name: Attraction between neutral molecules
statement: What causes the attraction between neutral molecules?
status_source: Timeline of atomic and subatomic physics: "Fritz London explains van der Waals forces as due to the interacting fluctuating dipole moments between molecules"

name: Isotopes as nuclear composition
statement: How can isotopes be explained in terms of nuclear constituents?
status_source: Timeline of atomic and subatomic physics: "Werner Heisenberg presents the proton-neutron model of the nucleus and uses it to explain isotopes"

name: Light from fast particles in liquids
statement: Why do relativistic particles in a liquid emit light?
status_source: Timeline of atomic and subatomic physics: "Pavel Cherenkov reports that light is emitted by relativistic particles traveling in a nonscintillating liquid"

name: Products of uranium bombarded with neutrons
statement: What elements form when uranium is bombarded with neutrons?
status_source: Timeline of atomic and subatomic physics: "Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann bombard uranium salts with thermal neutrons and discover barium among the reaction products"

name: Hydrogen level splitting
statement: Do the 2S and 2P levels of hydrogen have exactly the same energy?
status_source: Timeline of atomic and subatomic physics: "Willis Lamb and Robert Retherford measure the Lamb-Retherford shift"

name: Electron-positron bound state
statement: Can an electron and a positron form a bound atom?
status_source: Timeline of atomic and subatomic physics: "Martin Deutsch discovers positronium"

name: Wave nature of light
statement: Is light a wave?
status_source: Timeline of quantum mechanics: "Thomas Young establishes the wave nature of light with his double-slit experiment"

name: Regularity in hydrogen spectral lines
statement: Is there a numerical regularity in the visible spectral lines of hydrogen?
status_source: Timeline of quantum mechanics: "Johann Jakob Balmer discovers a numerical relationship between visible spectral lines of hydrogen"

name: Magnetic splitting of spectral lines
statement: Does a magnetic field split the emission lines of a light source?
status_source: Timeline of quantum mechanics: "Pieter Zeeman first observes the Zeeman splitting effect by applying a magnetic field to light sources"

name: Photoelectric effect
statement: How does light eject electrons from a metal?
status_source: Timeline of quantum mechanics: "Albert Einstein explains the photoelectric effect"

name: Interference at single-photon intensity
statement: Do interference patterns persist when only one photon is present at a time?
status_source: Timeline of quantum mechanics: "Geoffrey Ingram Taylor demonstrates that interference patterns of light were generated even when the light energy introduced consisted of only one photon"

name: Quantized atomic energy levels
statement: Are the energy levels of atoms quantized as the Bohr model asserts?
status_source: Timeline of quantum mechanics: "James Franck and Gustav Hertz report their experiment on electron collisions with mercury atoms"

name: Exclusion of identical fermions
statement: Why do electrons in an atom not all occupy the lowest quantum state?
status_source: Timeline of quantum mechanics: "Wolfgang Pauli outlines the 'Pauli exclusion principle'"

name: Limit on joint precision of position and momentum
statement: Is there a limit to knowing position and momentum at once?
status_source: Timeline of quantum mechanics: "Werner Heisenberg formulates the quantum uncertainty principle"

name: Quantitative theory of beta decay
statement: Can beta decay be described quantitatively with neutrino emission?
status_source: Timeline of quantum mechanics: "Fermi publishes a very successful model of beta decay in which neutrinos are produced"

name: Possibility of a nuclear chain reaction
statement: Is a self-sustaining nuclear chain reaction possible?
status_source: Timeline of quantum mechanics: "Leo Szilard and Fermi discover neutron multiplication in uranium, proving that a chain reaction is indeed possible"

name: Infinities in quantum electrodynamics
statement: How can the infinities in quantum electrodynamics be removed?
status_source: Timeline of quantum mechanics: "Sin-Itiro Tomonaga and Julian Schwinger independently introduce perturbative renormalization"

name: Equivalence of QED formulations
statement: Are Feynman's diagrams and the operator method of quantum electrodynamics equivalent?
status_source: Timeline of quantum mechanics: "Freeman Dyson determines the equivalence of two formulations of quantum electrodynamics"

name: Microwave amplification by stimulated emission
statement: Can microwaves be amplified by stimulated emission?
status_source: Timeline of quantum mechanics: "Charles H. Townes, collaborating with James P. Gordon, and Herbert J. Zeiger, builds the first ammonia maser"

name: Parity in the weak interaction
statement: Is parity conserved in the weak interaction?
status_source: Timeline of quantum mechanics: "Chien-Shiung Wu carries out the Wu Experiment, which observes parity violation in cobalt-60 decay"

name: Low-temperature superconductivity
statement: What explains superconductivity at low temperature?
status_source: Timeline of quantum mechanics: "John Bardeen, Leon Cooper and John Robert Schrieffer propose their quantum BCS theory of low temperature superconductivity"

name: Electron double-slit interference
statement: Do electrons show double-slit interference like light?
status_source: Timeline of quantum mechanics: "Claus Joensson performs Young's double-slit experiment for the first time with particles other than photons by using electrons"

name: Renormalizability of the electroweak theory
statement: Is the broken-symmetry electroweak gauge theory renormalizable?
status_source: Timeline of quantum mechanics: "Martinus J. G. Veltman and Gerardus 't Hooft show that, if the symmetries of Yang-Mills theory are broken according to the method suggested by Peter Higgs"

name: Cuprate high-temperature superconductivity
statement: Can superconductivity occur at temperatures far above those of classic metals?
status_source: Timeline of quantum mechanics: "Johannes Georg Bednorz and Karl Alexander Mueller produce unambiguous experimental proof of high-temperature superconductivity"

name: Bose-Einstein condensate in a dilute gas
statement: Can a pure Bose-Einstein condensate be made by cooling a dilute vapor?
status_source: Timeline of quantum mechanics: "Eric Cornell, Carl Wieman and Wolfgang Ketterle and co-workers at JILA create the first 'pure' Bose-Einstein condensate"

name: Pressure and volume of a gas
statement: How are the pressure and volume of a gas related?
status_source: Timeline of thermodynamics: "Robert Boyle experimentally discovers Boyle's law, relating the pressure and volume of a gas"

name: Absolute zero
statement: Is there a lowest possible temperature?
status_source: Timeline of thermodynamics: "Guillaume Amontons introduces the concept of absolute zero, based on observations of gases"

name: Heat absorbed by melting ice
statement: Does ice absorb heat while melting without changing temperature?
status_source: Timeline of thermodynamics: "Joseph Black discovers that ice absorbs heat without changing its temperature when melting"

name: Source of frictional heat
statement: What is the source of the heat produced by friction?
status_source: Timeline of thermodynamics: "Count Rumford (Benjamin Thompson) publishes his paper 'An Inquiry Concerning the Source of the Heat Which Is Excited by Friction'"

name: Volume and temperature of a gas
statement: How does the volume of a gas depend on its temperature?
status_source: Timeline of thermodynamics: "Joseph Louis Gay-Lussac publishes Charles's law"

name: Specific heat of crystals
statement: Is there a regularity in the specific heat capacity of crystals?
status_source: Timeline of thermodynamics: "Pierre Louis Dulong and Alexis Therese Petit give the Dulong-Petit law for the specific heat capacity of a crystal"

name: Efficiency limit of heat engines
statement: What limits the efficiency of a heat engine?
status_source: Timeline of thermodynamics: "Sadi Carnot analyzes the efficiency of steam engines using caloric theory"

name: Mechanical equivalent of heat
statement: How much mechanical work equals a unit of heat?
status_source: Timeline of thermodynamics: "James Joule experimentally finds the mechanical equivalent of heat"

name: Ideal gas law
statement: Can the gas laws be combined into one equation of state?
status_source: Timeline of thermodynamics: "Henri Victor Regnault added Avogadro's law to the combined gas law to produce the ideal gas law"

name: Conservation of energy
statement: Is energy conserved across all forms of heat and work?
status_source: Timeline of thermodynamics: "Hermann von Helmholtz publishes a definitive statement of the conservation of energy, the first law of thermodynamics"

name: Cooling of an expanding gas
statement: Does a rapidly expanding gas cool?
status_source: Timeline of thermodynamics: "Joule and Thomson demonstrate that a rapidly expanding gas cools"

name: Speed distribution of gas molecules
statement: What is the distribution of molecular speeds in a gas?
status_source: Timeline of thermodynamics: "James Clerk Maxwell discovers the distribution law of molecular velocities"

name: Universality of black-body emission
statement: Does the radiation from a black body depend only on temperature and frequency?
status_source: Timeline of thermodynamics: "Gustav Kirchhoff shows that energy emission from a black body is a function only of temperature and frequency"

name: State function for irreversibility
statement: Is there a state function that measures the irreversibility of heat processes?
status_source: Timeline of thermodynamics: "Clausius introduces the modern macroscopic concept of entropy"

name: Number of molecules in a volume of gas
statement: How many molecules are there in a given volume of gas?
status_source: Timeline of thermodynamics: "Josef Loschmidt applies Maxwell's theory to estimate the number-density of molecules in gases"

name: Equation of state of real gases
statement: What equation of state describes real gases and their liquefaction?
status_source: Timeline of thermodynamics: "Johannes Diderik van der Waals formulates his equation of state"

name: Entropy and probability
statement: How is entropy related to the number of molecular arrangements?
status_source: Timeline of thermodynamics: "Boltzmann states the relationship between entropy and probability"

name: Total radiation of a black body
statement: How does the total radiation of a black body scale with temperature?
status_source: Timeline of thermodynamics: "Josef Stefan observes that the total radiant flux from a blackbody is proportional to the fourth power of its temperature"

name: Response of equilibrium to perturbation
statement: How does a chemical system at equilibrium respond to a perturbation?
status_source: Timeline of thermodynamics: "Henri-Louis Le Chatelier states his principle that the response of a chemical system perturbed from equilibrium will be to counteract the perturbation"

name: Voltage of electrochemical cells
statement: How is the voltage of an electrochemical cell related to its chemical thermodynamics?
status_source: Timeline of thermodynamics: "Walther Nernst relates the voltage of electrochemical cells to their chemical thermodynamics via the Nernst equation"

name: Two kinds of electric charge
statement: Are there two kinds of electric charge?
status_source: Timeline of electromagnetism and classical optics: "C. F. du Fay and Francis Hauksbee the younger independently discover two kinds of frictional electricity"

name: Finite speed of light
statement: Is the speed of light finite?
status_source: Timeline of electromagnetism and classical optics: "Ole Roemer proves that speed of light is finite, by observing Jupiter's moons"

name: Nature of lightning
statement: Is lightning an electrical discharge?
status_source: Timeline of electromagnetism and classical optics: "Benjamin Franklin suggests flying a kite into a thunderstorm and transferring some of the charge into a Leyden jar"

name: Force law between electric charges
statement: What law governs the force between electric charges?
status_source: Timeline of electromagnetism and classical optics: "Joseph Priestley proposes an electrical inverse-square law"

name: Steady electric current from chemistry
statement: Can chemical action produce a steady electric current?
status_source: Timeline of electromagnetism and classical optics: "Alessandro Volta creates a voltaic cell producing an electric current by the chemical action"

name: Electrolysis of water
statement: Can electricity decompose water into its elements?
status_source: Timeline of electromagnetism and classical optics: "William Nicholson, Anthony Carlisle and Johann Ritter use electricity to decompose water into hydrogen and oxygen"

name: Force between current-carrying wires
statement: Do parallel current-carrying wires exert magnetic force on each other?
status_source: Timeline of electromagnetism and classical optics: "Andre-Marie Ampere demonstrates that parallel current-carrying wires experience magnetic force"

name: Bright spot behind a circular shadow
statement: Does diffraction put a bright spot at the centre of a circular shadow?
status_source: Timeline of electromagnetism and classical optics: "Francois Jean Dominique Arago verifies the existence of the Poisson-Arago bright spot"

name: Transverse nature of light
statement: Is light entirely transverse with no longitudinal vibration?
status_source: Timeline of electromagnetism and classical optics: "Augustin-Jean Fresnel derives a mathematical demonstration that polarization can be explained only if light is entirely transverse"

name: Direction of induced current
statement: Which way does an induced electric current flow?
status_source: Timeline of electromagnetism and classical optics: "Heinrich Lenz determines the direction of the induced electromotive force"

name: Magnetic influence on light
statement: Can a magnetic field change how light propagates in a material?
status_source: Timeline of electromagnetism and classical optics: "Michael Faraday discovers that light propagation in a material can be influenced by external magnetic fields"

name: Colour of the sky
statement: Why is the sky blue?
status_source: Timeline of electromagnetism and classical optics: "Lord Rayleigh discusses the blue sky law and sunsets"

name: Existence of electromagnetic waves
statement: Do the electromagnetic waves predicted by Maxwell exist?
status_source: Timeline of electromagnetism and classical optics: "Heinrich Hertz demonstrates the existence of electromagnetic waves"

name: Pressure of light
statement: Does light exert pressure on a solid body?
status_source: Timeline of electromagnetism and classical optics: "Pyotr Lebedev measures the pressure of light on a solid body"

name: Ultraviolet catastrophe
statement: Why does classical theory predict infinite black-body radiation at short wavelengths?
status_source: Timeline of electromagnetism and classical optics: "Max Planck resolves the ultraviolet catastrophe by suggesting that black-body radiation consists of discrete packets"

name: Equivalence of mass and energy
statement: Are mass and energy interchangeable?
status_source: Timeline of gravitational physics and relativity: "Albert Einstein discovers the equivalence of mass and energy, E = mc^2 in modern form"

name: Mercury perihelion precession
statement: What explains the anomalous precession of the perihelion of Mercury?
status_source: Timeline of gravitational physics and relativity: "Albert Einstein completes his general theory of relativity. He explains the perihelion of Mercury"

name: Exact solution for a spherical mass
statement: Is there an exact solution of the Einstein field equations for a spherical mass?
status_source: Timeline of gravitational physics and relativity: "Karl Schwarzschild publishes the Schwarzschild metric"

name: Uniqueness of the Schwarzschild solution
statement: Is the Schwarzschild solution the only spherically symmetric vacuum solution?
status_source: Timeline of gravitational physics and relativity: "George David Birkhoff proves Birkhoff's theorem on the uniqueness of the Schwarzschild solution"

name: Stable points of the three-body problem
statement: Where are the stable equilibrium points of the restricted three-body problem?
status_source: Timeline of gravitational physics and relativity: "Joseph-Louis Lagrange discovers the two remaining Lagrange points"

name: Speed of light on Earth
statement: Can the speed of light be measured on Earth?
status_source: Timeline of gravitational physics and relativity: "Armand Fizeau makes the first terrestrial determination of the speed of light"

name: Earth motion through the luminiferous aether
statement: Does the Earth move through a stationary luminiferous aether?
status_source: Timeline of Solar System astronomy: "The Michelson-Morley experiment, intended to measure the relative motion of Earth through the (assumed) stationary luminiferous aether, got no results"

name: Atomic model for spectral lines
statement: Can the spectral lines of atoms be explained by a quantum model?
status_source: Timeline of cosmological theories: "Niels Bohr publishes the Bohr model of the atom, which explains the spectral lines"

name: Spin of the electron
statement: Why do atomic spectra show doublet structure?
status_source: Timeline of atomic and subatomic physics: "George Uhlenbeck and Samuel Goudsmit postulate electron spin"

name: Matrix mechanics of atoms
statement: Can atomic spectra be computed from observable quantities alone?
status_source: Timeline of atomic and subatomic physics: "Werner Heisenberg, Max Born, and Pascual Jordan formulate quantum matrix mechanics"
